$comment: Authoritative test manifest. Each suite names the CLAIM it defends. A claim in README, PRODUCT.md or the interviewer brief that is not defended by a suite here is a claim we are not entitled to make.

defends: Records validate at the storage boundary, not in the MCP layer, so no write path bypasses validation.
Decisions and rejected approaches cannot be recorded without a rationale.
Supersession is single-successor, same-task, same-type, and never applies to an already-inactive record.
Nothing is ever deleted: a six-deep supersession chain retains all six records.
Superseded records leave recovery output but remain in the audit dump.
Task isolation: no record or recovery output crosses a task boundary.
Content is immutable; only status transitions are permitted in place.
A record cannot be born inactive; `transition` cannot reach `superseded` without a successor.
Every superseded record has exactly one successor, and exactly one record is the live head.
Task creation is atomic with its telemetry event.
State and telemetry survive closing the database and reopening the file in a new connection.
A v1 database migrates forward with data preserved and a usable backfilled ordering.
Migration is idempotent.
A database written by a newer schema version is refused rather than silently misread.
Twelve classes of secret are detected and redacted.
Ordinary engineering prose (file:line refs, git SHAs, benchmark numbers, URLs) produces zero false positives.
Redaction is deterministic and its output contains no residual secret.
content, rationale, evidence and the task objective are all scrubbed.
reject mode persists nothing at all.
No secret reaches recovery output.
DETERMINISM: identical requests produce byte-identical output; output is independent of wall-clock time and of record ids.
Ranking ties resolve on a total order, never on chance.
BOUNDING: a generous budget is respected; a tight budget drops material and says so in the output.
PROTECTED SET: blocking constraints, unmet acceptance criteria, rejected approaches and active decisions are never silently dropped; the budget is declared exceeded instead.
Advisory constraints and findings ARE droppable under pressure.
Every mandated section is present; an empty section says '(none recorded)' rather than vanishing.
Recovery emits a telemetry event, so utilisation is measurable.
Two connections to the same ledger file observe each other's writes.
Forty interleaved writes across two connections lose nothing and duplicate no ordinal.
A separate OS process writing the same ledger is observed after commit.
A rejected write leaves neither a record nor an event behind (transaction rollback), and the store stays usable.
PROTOCOL LEVEL: a real MCP Client and McpServer exchange JSON-RPC over the SDK transport.
Exactly the ten intended tools are exposed, each with a substantive description and an object input schema.
Read-only tools carry readOnlyHint; write tools do not.
Schema violations are rejected before the handler runs and write nothing.
Domain errors return a machine-readable code, not a protocol exception.
The recovery resource and the resume_task prompt return the same reconstruction as the tool.
REGRESSION: the reconstruction is present in structuredContent, not only in the text block (found by live agent integration).
REGRESSION: no tool declares an outputSchema whose payload is metadata only.
Every state change emits exactly one event, inside the same transaction as the write.
Events carry a session id, so cross-session behaviour is measurable.
Metrics with no data report null rather than a misleading zero.
Every metric declares its observability (direct / partial / self_reported) and carries an interpretation note.
constraint_violation_rate is declared SELF_REPORTED and must stay so.
Vanity metrics (records stored, MCP calls, tokens stored) are absent by test.
The session-reset experiment is reproducible: identical fingerprints, sufficiency scores and budget sweep across runs.
The baseline is not a strawman: it contains the ticket and the repository state and satisfies probes on its own.
The ledger condition is additive over the baseline, not a replacement for it.
NEGATIVE CONTROL: a fact never recorded in Session A is not recoverable — the ledger does not invent knowledge.
NEGATIVE CONTROL: a repository-only fact is not recoverable from the ledger alone.
Critical sufficiency survives every budget in the sweep, and budget pressure demonstrably costs non-critical material.

not_covered: Whether a real coding agent, given a sufficient resume context, actually behaves better. Sufficiency is a necessary condition and an upper bound. Closing this gap requires live agent runs against a held-out task set; the design is pre-registered in docs/agentdev-experiment.md.
Recall of the secret filter against real-world credential formats beyond the twelve classes tested. The filter is biased toward false positives and is documented as best-effort.
Behaviour under a ledger with tens of thousands of records. Selection is O(n) per recovery with no index-assisted ranking; the largest tested task holds low tens of records.
Multi-writer contention beyond two connections and one child process on one machine. Networked or NFS-backed SQLite is untested and unsupported.
